title: Derived direct image
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$, an integer $n\in\mathbf
Z_{\geq1}$, and put $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X,Y$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is
invertible, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; write $f_n$ for this morphism at
coefficient level $A_{E,n}$. On the small pro-etale sites
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with derived pullback and internal
Hom notation [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and derived tensor
notation [def-weil-derived-tensor], the functor
$f_*:\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to\Sh(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$
[def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] is left exact
[lem-weil-proetale-module-direct-image-left-exact]. At
finite level, choose a K-injective resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions] and
define its total right-derived functor
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] by

$$
 Rf_{*,n}=R(f_n)_*:D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})
 \longrightarrow D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n}).
$$

For a derived-complete integral [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]
complex $K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$, define

$$
 Rf_*K=
 R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{*,n}
 \bigl(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\bigr).
$$

Here $D(-,\mathcal O_E)$ and the restriction of scalars
$\operatorname{Res}_n$, applied termwise (it is exact
[lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact]), are those of the completed
coefficient sheaf [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and
$R\varprojlim_n$ is the derived limit [def-weil-derived-limit] in
$D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$, which exists because countable products
of pro-etale module sheaves are exact
[lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact, lem-weil-derived-limit-existence].
The tower maps are induced by $A_{E,n+1}\twoheadrightarrow A_{E,n}$: the map
$K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n+1}\to K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$,
followed by the identification of $R(f_{n+1})_*$ of an
$A_{E,n}$-module complex with $R(f_n)_*$ of it
[lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars]. The
finite-reduction comparison is the natural map

$$
 (Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}
 \longrightarrow
 Rf_{*,n}\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\bigr),
$$

adjoint [lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction] to the
projection of $R\varprojlim$ onto its $n$-th term;

its being an isomorphism, and its compatibility with composition and scalar
extension, are separate comparison assertions, not part of this definition of
the derived direct image. Here $A_{E,n}$ and finite-level constructibility
are the finite-torsion coefficient data
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and $\mathcal H^r$ is the
cohomology-sheaf functor [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. For
$\Lambda=E$ use the rationalized category
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]; for $\Lambda=\Qlb$ use the common-stage
category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

proof.text: The auxiliary completed structure map is the inverse-limit lift of the constant-section maps. Their naturality with respect to coefficient ring homomorphisms gives a map of the quotient inverse sequences. Ring-sheaf direct image preserves limits. Lift the resulting cone, then use the fully faithful forgetful functor from commutative ring sheaves to ring sheaves to retain commutativity. Joint monicity of the limit projections proves the stated uniqueness.

Completed module direct image is additive because its action on morphisms is the original sectionwise linear map. The finite projection identity identifies the scalar actions in the two ordinary restriction/direct-image composites. Identity on sections defines inverse linear maps, natural in the site object and the module; faithfulness of sections proves uniqueness.

Transport the completed and finite module categories to their AsSmall pro-etale sites. Realize scalar restriction and the completed structural-map pushforward as ringed-topos module direct images, with their actual module-functor equations. Apply the resolution clause of derived pushforward composition and transport back along the module equivalences. Thus completed direct image sends a K-injective resolution of the restriction of a finite-coefficient K-injective complex to a quasi-isomorphism. No preservation of K-injectivity by scalar restriction, and no invertibility of the inverse image of the completed coefficient ring map, is assumed.

Write F for finite direct image, G for completed direct image, and P,Q for exact coefficient restriction at source and target. The preceding resolution property makes D(P) followed by RG a right derived functor of P followed by G: its unit is invertible on K-injective representatives by naturality at the chosen resolution map. RF followed by D(Q) is a right derived functor of F followed by Q because Q is exact. Derive the identity-on-sections ordinary comparison and apply uniqueness of right derived functors. Their universal unit equations and unit naturality at the resolution map give exactly the published normalization. Cancel the invertible resolution factors on every K-injective representative to prove uniqueness there; naturality and existence of K-injective representatives prove uniqueness on every derived object. The existing finite-image tower, chosen Roos triangle and adjunct projection definitions then remain unchanged.

For arbitrary finite-type k-schemes use the coefficient-linear integral constructible adjunction. Reuse the proved raw scalar-localization construction rationalSystemPullback_isLeftAdjoint in SfRationalDirectImageAdjunction: localize functors, unit and counit, prove naturality by tensor induction and triangles on pure tensors, and identify the left functor with rationalDerivedPullback by its uniqueness specification. This supplies pointwise right adjoints at all finite coefficient stages, without a finite-field presentation.

Apply the generalized coefficient compatibility theorem to obtain the unique normalized left stage morphism and invertible right mates for the already proved pointwise adjunctions. Mathlib mateEquiv_counit supplies the actual counit equation. Reuse the fully proved generic helpers DirectImageAdjunction.mateFamily, mateFamilyUnit and mateFamilyCounit in SfCommonStageDirectImage: the counit equation implies right-family coherence and compatible units. Descend these maps with the stage-system functor construction; finite-stage triangle identities prove both descended triangles. The normalized representative formulas identify the descended left functor with commonStageDerivedPullback by commonStageDerivedPullback_existsUnique. Its right adjoint and specifying adjunction are therefore the existing geometricCommonStageDirectImage and geometricCommonStageAdjunction definitions.

proof_origin.place: 6.7.2, 6.8.14 and 6.8.15; retain the existing finite/integral construction steps and add the arbitrary-field rational adjunction and formal stage descent. Generic previously proved helpers are reused through private imports, without changing their declarations.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against the master blueprint node (order 1468); slopmaster2 has no Lean for it (state none) and no separate blueprint file for this node. The mathematical content is unchanged; the statement now names every notion it is built from, by bracketed references added to its existing sentences: the underived direct image of pro-etale module sheaves (new node def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image) and its left exactness (new lem-weil-proetale-module-direct-image-left-exact); the K-injective resolutions (def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions) and the finite-level derived direct image $R(f_n)_*$, which is $Ru_*$ of def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations with $u=f$ and coefficients $A_{E,n}$; $D(-,\mathcal O_E)$ and $\operatorname{Res}_n$ (def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, being split by another worker) with the exactness that lets $\operatorname{Res}_n$ act termwise on derived categories (lem-weil-restriction-of-scalars-exact); $R\varprojlim$ as the Roos-triangle derived limit (def-weil-derived-limit), whose existence needs countable products in $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ (lem-weil-derived-limit-existence part 2, with the exactness of countable products of pro-etale module sheaves, new lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact from Bhatt-Scholze 3.1.9, 3.2.3, 4.2.8); the tower maps, which need the identification of $R(f_{n+1})_*$ on $A_{E,n}$-complexes with $R(f_n)_*$ (new lem-weil-proetale-direct-image-restriction-of-scalars, Stacks 0D6E); and the finite-reduction comparison map, defined as the adjoint of the projection $R\varprojlim\to$ $n$-th term under $-\otimes^L A_{E,n}\dashv\operatorname{Res}_n$ (new lem-weil-derived-scalar-extension-restriction-adjunction, Stacks 07A6). Kept the blueprint's dependencies (scheme morphisms, pro-etale site, derived pullback/tensor/Hom notation, derived tensor, $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$, finite-torsion constructibility, cohomology sheaves, rationalized and common-stage categories). Mathlib has abstract total right derived functors, K-injective complexes, pushforward of sheaves along continuous functors and the small pro-etale site, but not the pro-etale base-change functor, unbounded K-injective resolutions of sheaves, or derived limits; searches recorded.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, with coefficient sheaves
$\Lambda_W=p_W^*\Lambda$; the cases of interest are $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$
for a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with uniformizer $\pi_E$, an integer
$n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\pi_E^n$. Let $X,Y$ be schemes and let
$f:X\to Y$ be a morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-étale sites
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with derived pullback and internal Hom
notation [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and derived tensor notation
[def-weil-derived-tensor], the pushforward of module objects
$f_*:\Mod_{\Lambda_X}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$
([det-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]) is left exact. Its total right
derived functor, computed by K-injective resolutions
([det-def-sfb-derived-categories]), is

$$
 Rf_*:D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\longrightarrow D(Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda);
$$

it is right adjoint to the derived pullback $Lf^*$ of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and,
restriction of scalars along $\eta_f$ being exact, it is the right derived functor of the
transport $\operatorname{mapMod}(f^{\Ab}_*)$ followed by termwise restriction of scalars along
$\eta_f$.

The definition is the same for every $\Lambda$; for
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, where $(A_{E,n})_W$ is the classical constant sheaf, write
$f_n$ for $f$ with these coefficients and $Rf_{*,n}=R(f_n)_*$. Here $A_{E,n}$
and finite-level constructibility are the finite-torsion coefficient data
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and $\mathcal H^r$ is the
cohomology-sheaf functor [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ the projection-formula map

$$
 (Rf_*K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{E,Y}}(A_{E,n})_Y
 \longrightarrow
 Rf_{*,n}\bigl(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(A_{E,n})_X\bigr)
$$

is an isomorphism, and for derived $\pi_E$-complete $K$ one has
$Rf_*K\simeq R\varprojlim_nRf_{*,n}(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_{E,X}}(A_{E,n})_X)$.
These are consequences of the definition, proved in
[prop-weil-pbc-direct-image-limits]; they are not used to define $Rf_*$.
